messages:
clare: kicking off a short thread to land a single canonical handover pattern across hosted/dedicated/private. current options (sidecar, runtime endpoint, install manifest) are splintering our router logic. proposal: define an 'adapter-handshake' plus ephemeral 'admission-ticket' flow as the canonical interface.

marc: can you sketch difference vs what we already have? trying to avoid rebranding trivia.

clare: sure. adapter-handshake = a simple bootstrap endpoint + signed bootstrap manifest (install-time) the runtime ships or stores. admission-ticket = short-lived JWS the control-plane mints after validating the handshake. ticket contains capability vector, tenant_hmac, and binding claims. key idea: routers accept tickets as admission proof and treat sidecars as an optional local adapter, not a requirement.

yuki: security note: tickets must be bound to either mTLS peer cert or include a nonce keyed to a recent probe to avoid replay. recommend default TTL 45s and single-use flag optional.

samir: operational variants: hosted -> control-plane mints and validates tickets centrally. dedicated -> same but routing respects reservation commitments first. private/on-prem -> operator can either upload signed bootstrap manifest or allow control-plane probe + ticket minting via a management channel. if air-gapped, allow operator to push tickets using CLI signed by their key.

ops: please call out fallback modes explicitly. operators need a clear path for installs that cannot reach control-plane.

clare: fallback modes: (1) manifest-only: runtime reads a signed bootstrap_manifest.json at install and accepts that as baseline capabilities; (2) operator-push: operator runs redwoodctl to request a ticket and POST it into the runtime; (3) sidecar-assisted: sidecar provides local cache and enforces tickets. manifest-only is least dynamic; operator-push enables ephemeral tickets without outbound runtime connectivity.

marc: cryptography: bootstrap_manifest should be a detached JWS with claims: issuer, tenant_hash, capabilities[], issued_at, expires_at, kid, revocation_endpoint. admission_ticket is a compact JWS including ticket_id, tenant_hmac, capabilities_fingerprint, exp, iat, binding_claim. tickets signed by control-plane KMS by default or by customer-KMS if provided.

yuki: observability: emit metrics with tenant_hmac label only. metric names: adapter.handshake.success, adapter.ticket.issued, adapter.ticket.accepted, adapter.capability.flip. include attestation_level label: manifest|operator_push|attested_probe. do not emit plaintext tenant ids.

samir: routing semantics: tickets are admission tokens, not request auth. runtimes must still verify per-request tenant tokens. router decision order: 1) reservation constraints (dedicated) -> 2) ticket attestation level + capability_vector -> 3) tenant policy. If no ticket, fall back to manifest-only route or conservative baseline models.

ops: downgrade behavior: if capability flips from present->absent in accepted tickets, router should demote new sessions immediately, preserve existing sessions for a configurable grace_period (default 30s), then evict. re-enablement requires N consecutive successful handshakes (default N=2) to avoid flapping.

marc: replay prevention: prefer binding to mTLS peer if available. if not, include request_nonce signed into ticket and verify nonce on acceptance. if neither is present, force TTL <= 30s and add anomaly scoring.

yuki: sidecar tradeoffs: sidecar provides local caching (prefix cache, offline retry) and richer telemetry enrichment. downsides: extra binary lifecycle and upgrade churn. in-scope for sidecar-only features we should list them explicitly in RFC.

clare: initial feature mapping proposal (quick):
- local-prefix-cache -> sidecar required
- offline-retry/session-pinning -> sidecar recommended
- streaming generation -> ticket-only OK
- quantization-aware routing -> ticket or manifest OK (depends on attestation)

samir: we should document what attestation_level maps to routing privileges. rough idea: manifest (low), operator_push (medium), attested_probe (high). attested_probe requires HSM/KMS-backed signing and an attestation claim.

ops: operators will ask how to rotate keys and revoke tickets. please be explicit: manifest keys rotate at admin cadence (suggest 90d), ticket signing keys rotated weekly, and we publish a revocation list for manifest KIDs and ticket signing KIDs. runtimes must reject tickets signed by revoked keys.

marc: audit requirements: tickets and handshake events must be written to append-only audit stream with signature_kid and issued_by. include revocation events and audit-proof links.

yuki: metrics to add for early detection: adapter.capability.inconsistency_count (when manifest vs accepted ticket disagree), adapter.ticket.latency (probe->ticket issuance->accept), routing.demote_events. correlate traces: handshake->ticket->request.

samir: corner case: partial capability removal (e.g., kv-cache still present but turbo-quant module gone). router should consider per-capability state and only demote variants that require the missing capability. avoid global demote unless a critical capability is lost.

clare: good call. add per-capability grace TTLs in RFC. propose default table: kv-cache 30s, hardware-accel 60s, quantization 45s. configurable per-tenant.

ops: ergonomics: expose redwoodctl commands: `redwoodctl handshake probe --runtime <addr>` and `redwoodctl ticket push --file ticket.jws` for operator-push flow. document exact HTTP endpoints for runtimes: GET /internal/v1/handshake, POST /internal/v1/tickets. require auth for push via operator token.

marc: security review requested: @sec-bot please verify claims, replay resistance, revocation model.

sec-bot: acknowledged. will review threat model and propose mandatory claims and verification steps. recommend including TLS cert pinning when possible.

clare: next steps: I'll draft RFC titled "adapter-handshake + admission-ticket" with sequence diagrams, endpoints, sample JWS payloads, feature matrix, and routing state machine. schedule review next Wed. any objections to the name?

marc: no objections. +1 pending security checklist.

samir: +1. I'll add KMS appendix.

yuki: +1. will include telemetry appendix.

clare: thanks all — pulling into docs and creating INF-4342 to track implementation tasks.
